paragraphs: Training a large neural network requires memory for intermediate calculations as well as model parameters. Gradient checkpointing reduces this memory demand by recomputing some intermediate results when they are needed. The central planning problem is deciding which results to keep and which to calculate again, balancing memory savings against additional computation.

The paper introduces FastSA, a recomputation algorithm based on simulated annealing. This heuristic searches for useful plans without relying on the mixed integer or constraint programming approaches used by the compared systems. Those approaches face exponentially large search spaces, which limits how well they scale to large computational graphs.

FastSA optimizes graphs containing thousands of nodes in 3 to 30 seconds and produces solutions comparable to or better than the alternatives studied. Tests on PyTorch vision and text models, including transformers, report average memory reductions of 73% with 18% extra computation. These results support the practical value of quickly finding favorable memory–computation tradeoffs for large-model training.
neurips-2023-a-fast-heuristic-to-optimiz.tldr: FastSA quickly finds recomputation plans that substantially reduce training memory while adding modest computation in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: Image restoration requires an output that looks natural while remaining faithful to the image being repaired. A diffusion model’s ability to generate realistic images does not by itself solve that problem. This paper focuses on how restoration information should guide the generation process throughout the network.

The framework first uses a lightweight UNet to produce an initial estimate. The diffusion model then learns the residual: the correction needed relative to that estimate. Specially designed modules introduce both the initial guidance and additional conditioning information into every diffusion block. This allows the influence of the guidance to vary across image locations.

For high-resolution inputs, the authors introduce a patch-splitting strategy applied between sampling steps, reporting arbitrary-resolution outputs without grid artifacts. They evaluate the framework on extreme low-light denoising, deblurring, and JPEG restoration. The reported perceptual improvements across these tasks support the usefulness of combining an initial restoration estimate with spatially adaptive guidance throughout diffusion.
neurips-2023-a-unified-conditional-frame.tldr: The framework restores images by guiding every diffusion block with an initial estimate and learning the corrections that estimate needs.

paragraphs: Parsing asks a model to turn language into a structured representation of syntax or meaning. Language models can generate such representations, but their outputs must obey the rules of the target format. BenchCLAMP provides a common setting for testing language models when those rules constrain generation.

The benchmark supplies context-free grammars for seven semantic parsing datasets and two syntactic parsing datasets. A shared decoding interface restricts outputs to representations covered by those grammars. Each dataset also has low-, medium-, and high-resource splits, allowing comparisons across different amounts of training data. Both prompting and fine-tuning are supported within this evaluation setup.

The authors evaluate seven language models, including two GPT-3 variants accessed through an API. Their experiments show that pretrained encoder-decoder models can match or outperform state-of-the-art parsing methods when decoding is constrained. The contribution combines an evaluation resource with evidence that enforcing output structure can make general language models competitive on both kinds of parsing.
neurips-2023-benchclamp-a-benchmark-for-.tldr: BenchCLAMP standardizes evaluation of language models for parsing with grammar-constrained outputs across datasets and data budgets.

paragraphs: Evaluating adversarial robustness requires knowing how much robustness is possible for the data and allowed attacks. A classifier’s errors may reflect weaknesses in training, but some errors may remain unavoidable even for the best possible classifier. This paper studies that distinction for classification with multiple classes and a test-time attacker.

The authors construct a conflict hypergraph from a discrete dataset and the attacker’s permitted changes. This structure represents conflicts that constrain robust classification and supports a general formulation of the optimal 0–1 loss, which counts incorrect predictions. The framework yields achievable information-theoretic lower bounds for multi-class classifiers on any discrete dataset.

Computing the full formulation is prohibitively expensive in practice. The paper therefore develops alternative attacker–classifier games that more efficiently bound the range containing the optimum. Evaluations on benchmark datasets use these results to analyze the gap between trained classifiers and optimal robustness. This makes the framework a diagnostic tool for separating training shortcomings from limits imposed by the classification problem.
neurips-2023-characterizing-the-optimal-.tldr: A conflict-hypergraph framework characterizes optimal adversarial classification loss and helps measure how far trained multi-class classifiers fall short.

paragraphs: Few-shot learning adapts a model to unfamiliar categories using limited examples. On these new categories, feature values across channels can become relatively concentrated, making channel importance difficult to distinguish. The paper argues that common geometric comparisons, such as cosine similarity and Euclidean distance, can then treat semantically different features as similar.

DiffKendall compares the importance ordering of feature channels using Kendall’s rank correlation. The authors find that substituting this ranking-based comparison only at inference improves performance across a range of existing methods and datasets from different domains. This suggests that the ordering of channels can carry useful information that geometric similarity does not reliably capture.

To use the same idea during meta-training, the paper introduces a differentiable loss that addresses the original rank correlation’s non-differentiability. The resulting comparison can be incorporated into numerous few-shot methods that currently use geometric similarity. Extensive experiments report significant improvements, supporting rank-based comparison as both an inference modification and a component of training.
neurips-2023-diffkendall-a-novel-approac.tldr: DiffKendall improves few-shot learning by comparing feature-channel rankings and making that comparison differentiable for training.

paragraphs: Anomaly detection requires learning what belongs to the training distribution and distinguishing samples that fall outside it. This paper trains an energy-based model by using the low-dimensional structure within the data. Its central idea is to make training examples reflect meaningful variations near that structure.

The proposed Manifold Projection-Diffusion Recovery method first perturbs a data point along a low-dimensional manifold approximating the training dataset. It then trains the model to assign high probability to recovering the original point. Training still uses Markov chain Monte Carlo to generate negative samples, but draws them from a distribution concentrated near the manifold.

These nearby negative samples are informative because they reflect relevant ways the data can vary. The authors report that the resulting energy function learns accurate boundaries of the training distribution and detects out-of-distribution samples effectively. Experiments cover images, vectors, and acoustic signals, showing strong performance across these data types. The findings support using data geometry to shape the negative examples used in anomaly-detection training.
neurips-2023-energy-based-models-for-ano.tldr: MPDR trains anomaly detectors through recovery from manifold-based perturbations, using informative negative samples near the data’s low-dimensional structure.

paragraphs: Dynamic graphs contain relationships that evolve over time, and their patterns can change when the surrounding environment changes. A model trained in one setting may consequently struggle in another. This paper treats hidden environments as an explicit part of learning how to generalize across such distribution shifts.

The EAGLE framework first uses an environment-aware dynamic graph network to separate environmental influences through multiple channels. It then creates diverse environment instances from inferred distributions. An invariant-pattern recognition mechanism seeks spatial and temporal patterns that remain useful across these environments, while node-level causal interventions use mixtures of the instantiated environment samples.

The approach links environment inference with the search for stable predictive structure. Its purpose is to help prediction rely on patterns that survive changes in the conditions generating the graph. Experiments on real-world and synthetic dynamic graphs report better performance than state-of-the-art baselines under distribution shifts. These results support the proposed environment-learning perspective for the evaluated out-of-distribution settings.
neurips-2023-environment-aware-dynamic-g.tldr: EAGLE models hidden environments in dynamic graphs to learn spatial and temporal patterns that transfer better under distribution shifts.

paragraphs: Identifying an object in a 3D scene from a language description can require understanding other objects and their relationships. The target’s own appearance may not provide enough information to distinguish it within a complex scene. CORE-3DVG addresses this contextual reasoning problem while also handling the absence of annotations for contextual objects and relations.

The model divides grounding into three sequential networks. A text-guided object detector identifies relevant objects, a relation-matching network considers their relationships, and a target-identification network selects the referred object. This modular sequence makes context an explicit part of the path from a description to its intended target.

During training, the system generates pseudo-labels to help learn contextual objects and uses weak supervision to learn relations. These techniques provide learning signals where direct contextual annotations are unavailable. Evaluations on Nr3D, Sr3D, and ScanRefer report state-of-the-art performance. The findings support explicitly learning contextual objects and relationships as a way to improve language-guided object identification in 3D scenes.
neurips-2023-exploiting-contextual-objec.tldr: CORE-3DVG improves language-guided object identification in 3D scenes by explicitly learning contextual objects and their relationships.

paragraphs: Structured representation learning aims to separate meaningful factors of variation within a model’s internal representation. The paper argues that existing disentangled and equivariant approaches can be insufficiently specified or flexible for realistic factors. It proposes organizing representations around distinct transformations expressed as flows through latent space.

The generative model defines separate probability paths for different input transformations. Each flow follows the gradient field of a learned potential under dynamic optimal transport. This provides a way to describe how a representation changes under a transformation, connecting the separation of factors with the goal of having latent changes correspond to changes in the input.

On standard representation-learning benchmarks, the model achieves higher likelihoods while moving closer to approximate equivariance. The authors also demonstrate that learned transformations can be composed flexibly and extrapolated to new data. These findings suggest a degree of robustness and generalizability, alongside a more useful organization of the learned representation. The claim concerns the demonstrated structure and transfer, rather than complete separation of every possible factor.
neurips-2023-flow-factorized-representat.tldr: The method structures latent representations through learned transformation flows that compose flexibly and show improved likelihood and approximate equivariance.

paragraphs: A model may be trained on only a small portion of the classes it could encounter. When distances between labels are available, those relationships provide information beyond the model’s original training labels. Loki uses this label-space geometry to adapt predictions without additional training.

The method replaces the usual argmax prediction rule with a Fréchet mean, a notion of a mean defined using distances in the label space. The paper analyzes how label-space diameter, sample complexity, and model dimension interact. It also characterizes when unobserved classes can be predicted and develops a class-selection procedure for cases where the entire unseen label range cannot be reached.

Using external metrics, Loki reports up to 29.7% relative improvement over SimCLR on ImageNet and scales to hundreds of thousands of classes. When external metrics are unavailable, distances derived from class embeddings yield a reported 10.5% improvement on pretrained zero-shot models such as CLIP. The results show how changing the final prediction rule can make existing model outputs more useful.
neurips-2023-geometry-aware-adaptation-f.tldr: Loki uses distances between labels to adapt pretrained predictions to new classes or improve zero-shot performance without further training.

paragraphs: Randomized smoothing builds robustness guarantees around a classifier’s majority prediction when random noise is added to its input. Complex inputs, however, contain individual entities such as image pixels or graph nodes. When an attacker can modify only a subset of those entities, smoothing the whole object presents a distinct certification challenge.

Hierarchical randomized smoothing introduces randomness at two levels: it randomly selects a subset of entities and then adds noise only to that subset. This more targeted perturbation scheme is designed around the structure of the attack. The authors instantiate it with different noise distributions to derive robustness certificates for both discrete and continuous data.

The paper reports stronger robustness guarantees while maintaining high accuracy. Experiments on image classification and node classification show better robustness–accuracy tradeoffs than the compared approaches. The significance is that the way certification noise is distributed across an input matters: accounting for attacks on subsets of entities can improve the guarantees obtained for the evaluated classification problems.
neurips-2023-hierarchical-randomized-smo.tldr: Hierarchical randomized smoothing improves robustness certification by adding noise only to a randomly selected subset of an input’s entities.

paragraphs: Variational inference approximates a target distribution using a distribution that can be learned. Semi-implicit variational inference expands the available approximation families through hierarchical construction, but its commonly used single layer can struggle with complicated target structure. This paper extends that construction to multiple layers.

The proposed HSIVI method introduces auxiliary distributions between a simple starting distribution and the target. Conditional layers are trained progressively to match these intermediate distributions. This breaks the overall approximation into a sequence of distribution-matching problems, giving the model a richer way to represent complex targets.

The authors demonstrate increased expressiveness on several Bayesian inference problems. They also apply HSIVI to accelerate diffusion sampling when pretrained score networks are available, using a score-matching objective. Across the tested datasets, the resulting sampler produces high-quality samples comparable to or better than existing fast diffusion samplers with few function evaluations. The contribution therefore connects a more expressive inference family with an application to reducing diffusion sampling work.
neurips-2023-hierarchical-semi-implicit-.tldr: HSIVI learns multilayer distribution approximations that improve Bayesian inference expressiveness and can accelerate diffusion sampling using pretrained score networks.

paragraphs: A contextual bandit must choose actions while learning from their rewards, balancing information gathering with using what it already knows. This paper studies a linear version in which the number of features exceeds the interaction budget and may even be infinite. It does not assume that only a few regression coefficients are nonzero.

Instead, the analysis uses a small-effective-rank condition on the data distribution. This provides structure for studying a minimum-norm interpolating estimator in the overparameterized setting. The proposed explore-then-commit algorithm first gathers information and then commits to decisions based on what it has learned.

The authors derive an optimal rate for this explore-then-commit algorithm as a function of the budget and show how balancing exploration and exploitation achieves it. They also introduce an adaptive version that finds the balance automatically and assess both algorithms through simulations. The work shows how distributional structure can support analysis without coefficient sparsity in this high-dimensional bandit setting.
neurips-2023-high-dimensional-contextual.tldr: The paper analyzes high-dimensional contextual bandits without coefficient sparsity by using small effective rank and adaptively balancing exploration with commitment.

paragraphs: Offline reinforcement learning learns a policy from an existing dataset, which may provide insufficient coverage of the environment. A-Crab addresses this setting by making policy evaluation conservative relative to the available data. Its target is the best policy covered by that dataset.

The algorithm combines marginalized importance sampling with an actor–critic structure. The actor supplies a policy, while the critic evaluates it pessimistically and keeps its average importance-weighted Bellman error small. This error measures consistency in the critic’s value estimates, with importance weighting incorporated into the average. The method uses an average notion of policy coverage that exploits visitation structure and is weaker than the worst-case coverage condition discussed in the paper.

The analysis establishes the optimal statistical rate of 1/√N for convergence to the best covered policy, including with general function approximators. The authors also report improvement over the data-collection policy across a wide range of particular hyperparameters. Theory and experiments together support this combination of conservative evaluation, importance weighting, and actor–critic learning.
neurips-2023-importance-weighted-actor-c.tldr: A-Crab combines conservative actor–critic evaluation with importance weighting to learn the best dataset-covered policy at an optimal statistical rate.

paragraphs: Understanding generated images involves recognizing both their content and their style. The paper argues that synthetic images introduce substantial diversity along these dimensions, making it uncertain how well existing vision-language models understand them. JourneyDB provides a dedicated resource for examining that capability.

The dataset contains four million generated images paired with the text prompts used to create them. An additional external subset includes outputs from another 22 text-to-image models, broadening the benchmark’s coverage of image generators. These paired images and prompts provide a basis for evaluating different aspects of generated-image comprehension.

The authors define four tasks: recovering prompts from images, retrieving images by style, writing captions, and answering visual questions. Together, these tasks examine both what an image depicts and how it is presented. Evaluations of state-of-the-art multimodal models analyze their strengths and limitations on the dataset. The contribution is a shared benchmark for studying generated-content understanding, alongside an initial assessment of existing models.
neurips-2023-journeydb-a-benchmark-for-g.tldr: JourneyDB pairs four million generated images with their prompts and introduces four benchmarks for understanding synthetic image content and style.

paragraphs: Routing solvers search for good routes while respecting problem constraints. Neural search methods often mask out moves that would violate those constraints, restricting where the search can go. This paper introduces NeuOpt and a guided strategy that allows exploration of both feasible and infeasible regions.

NeuOpt learns flexible k-opt exchanges, which modify routes through exchanges involving multiple connections. A tailored action factorization and recurrent dual-stream decoder represent these moves. The Guided Infeasible Region Exploration scheme adds feasibility information to the policy network and shapes reinforcement-learning rewards to steer exploration. Dynamic Data Augmentation further diversifies searches at inference time.

Experiments on the Traveling Salesman Problem and Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem report substantial gains over existing masking-based learning-to-search methods. The authors also report superiority over the evaluated learning-to-construct and learning-to-predict solvers. The findings support treating constraint handling as part of a learned search strategy, with explicit guidance for exploring infeasible regions, rather than limiting the search entirely through feasibility masks.
neurips-2023-learning-to-search-feasible.tldr: NeuOpt learns flexible route exchanges and uses feasibility-aware rewards to search both feasible and infeasible regions effectively.

paragraphs: Agents estimating the same normal-distribution mean can reduce collection costs by sharing independent samples. But simple pooling creates incentives to contribute too little or fabricate observations. The paper designs a collaboration mechanism that accounts for these strategic choices while seeking accurate estimates at low collective cost.

When returning other participants’ data to an agent, the mechanism adds corruption in proportion to how much that agent’s report differs from the others. It pairs this rule with minimax-optimal estimators for the corrupted data. The value of the information an agent receives is therefore tied to its contribution, creating incentives within the collaboration.

The mechanism is Nash incentive compatible and individually rational, and its combined estimation-error and collection-cost penalty is at most twice the global minimum. An extension to high-dimensional, non-Gaussian distributions with bounded variance retains the three stated properties with weaker results. In two special cases with restricted agent strategies, alternative mechanisms essentially achieve the global minimum. The guarantees thus connect statistical estimation quality with participants’ incentives.
neurips-2023-mechanism-design-for-collab.tldr: The paper designs incentive-compatible data sharing for mean estimation with total error and collection cost within twice the global optimum.

paragraphs: Benign overfitting describes the possibility that an overparameterized model generalizes well despite fitting its training data very closely. Kernel regression is relevant because it can approximate the generalization behavior of neural networks in the lazy-training regime. This paper studies how kernel ridge regression’s excess prediction risk behaves asymptotically.

The analysis assumes power-law decay for the kernel eigenvalues and the target function. Under assumptions described as mild and more realistic than Gaussian design, it rigorously characterizes the learning curve. That curve captures how the regularization choice, the target’s source condition, and observation noise interact in determining excess risk.

This gives a formal account of relationships that earlier learning-curve arguments often treated heuristically. In particular, the results suggest that benign overfitting in overparameterized neural networks occurs only when noise is small. That implication is presented as a suggestion from the analysis, with the neural-network connection grounded in the kernel approximation. The contribution is an asymptotic characterization under the stated decay conditions.
neurips-2023-on-the-asymptotic-learning-.tldr: Under power-law decay conditions, the paper rigorously characterizes kernel ridge regression learning curves and suggests small noise is needed for benign overfitting.

paragraphs: Stein Variational Gradient Descent represents a target distribution using particles. Its idealized infinite-particle behavior is well understood, but guarantees for a finite collection are harder to establish. This paper introduces virtual particles to connect the population-level dynamics with algorithms that can be implemented using finitely many particles.

The resulting methods, VP-SVGD and GB-SVGD, are computationally efficient random-batch approximations. Under standard assumptions, their output particles are at least as good as independent samples from a distribution whose Kernel Stein Discrepancy to the target is bounded by O(d^(1/3)/(KT)^(1/6)), where K is batch size and T is the number of steps.

The results also hold under a mild growth condition on the potential function, weaker than conditions commonly used in previous analyses. The authors derive empirical-measure convergence with a double-exponential improvement over the best known finite-particle SVGD analysis. They also obtain oracle complexities with polynomial dimension dependence. These are improvements in theoretical guarantees, connecting practical finite-particle computation to population-level analysis without the previously exponential dimension dependence.
neurips-2023-provably-fast-finite-partic.tldr: Virtual-particle constructions yield efficient finite-particle SVGD variants with substantially improved convergence guarantees and polynomial dimension dependence.

paragraphs: Generalization guarantees describe how learning from a sample relates to performance beyond that sample. Information-theoretic bounds provide one way to formalize this relationship, but their usefulness depends on how tightly they capture the learning situation. This paper develops a new framework for obtaining sharper guarantees in several settings.

The construction centers on a neighboring-hypothesis matrix and a family of notions called sample-conditioned hypothesis stability. These provide a new way to organize the hypotheses considered in the analysis and express stability with reference to the sample. Together, they form the basis for the paper’s improved information-theoretic bounds.

The authors report improvements over previous bounds in various learning scenarios, with particular attention to stochastic convex optimization. In that setting, their guarantees address limitations identified in earlier information-theoretic analyses. The stated advance is therefore about the strength of the mathematical account of generalization: a more informative stability formulation leads to tighter guarantees in the scenarios analyzed. The abstract does not claim a universal improvement across every learning problem.
neurips-2023-sample-conditioned-hypothes.tldr: A neighboring-hypothesis matrix and sample-conditioned stability yield sharper information-theoretic generalization bounds, including for stochastic convex optimization.

paragraphs: Neural-network optimization can become unstable when the underlying loss landscape produces nonmonotone behavior. This paper studies linear interpolation as a principled way to stabilize training. Its analysis uses nonexpansive operators, connecting the interpolation step to mathematical properties that support convergence.

The authors construct relaxed approximate proximal point, or RAPP. Within the 1-SCLI method class, they establish the first last-iterate convergence rates for ρ-comonotone problems under the condition ρ > −1/(2L). Last-iterate guarantees concern the final optimization iterate itself. The construction also extends to problems with constraints or regularization.

Changing RAPP’s inner optimizer recovers the Lookahead family. The paper proves convergence for Lookahead on cohypomonotone problems even with gradient descent ascent as its base optimizer, and broadens the covered problem range by using properties inherited from that optimizer. Experiments on generative adversarial networks support the benefits of interpolation in both RAPP and Lookahead. The theoretical guarantees apply to the specified problem classes and conditions.
neurips-2023-stable-nonconvex-nonconcave.tldr: The paper gives conditional convergence guarantees for interpolation-based RAPP and Lookahead optimizers and demonstrates benefits in GAN training.

paragraphs: Prediction problems with many sparse features often depend on interactions between features, making the choice of interactions an important part of deep sparse networks. Previous approaches have mainly searched at a coarse level. This paper asks how interaction selection can also account for finer distinctions within the features.

The proposed approach selects interactions at both the feature-field and feature-value levels. Combining these levels creates a large search space, so the authors introduce a decomposed representation of that space that is calculated as needed. Their OptFeature algorithm uses this construction to select field-level and value-level interactions simultaneously.

The design addresses the practical challenge of exploring finer interactions without losing the ability to search efficiently. Experiments on three large real-world benchmark datasets report good accuracy and efficiency, while additional studies support the method’s feasibility. These findings provide empirical support for hybrid-grained selection: considering both broad feature groupings and individual values can be practical within the evaluated deep sparse networks.
neurips-2023-towards-hybrid-grained-feat.tldr: OptFeature efficiently selects feature interactions at both field and value levels using an on-demand decomposed search space.

paragraphs: The paper identifies an empirical pattern in graph anomaly datasets: normal nodes tend to resemble and connect strongly with one another, while abnormal nodes show substantially weaker homophily. It uses this difference to build an unsupervised anomaly score based on how closely each node resembles its neighbors.

Truncated Affinity Maximization learns representations by increasing local affinity, defined through similarity of node attributes or representations. Nodes with lower affinity receive higher anomaly scores. Because edges between normal and abnormal nodes can bias training, the method iteratively removes non-homophily edges and optimizes on the resulting truncated graphs.

The learned representations give normal nodes substantially stronger local affinity than abnormal nodes. Across ten real-world datasets, TAM outperforms seven competing models, with reported increases exceeding 10% in AUROC/AUPRC over the best contenders on challenging datasets. The results support exploiting the observed asymmetry in neighborhood similarity as an anomaly signal, while modifying the graph to reduce interference from edges that work against that signal.
neurips-2023-truncated-affinity-maximiza.tldr: TAM detects graph anomalies through weak neighborhood affinity and learns clearer representations by iteratively removing non-homophily edges.

paragraphs: Diffusion models generate images through repeated evaluations of a denoising network, making sampling expensive. Reducing the number of evaluations can compromise image quality, especially when very few steps are available. UniPC addresses this tradeoff through a predictor–corrector formulation for sampling.

The authors first derive UniC, a corrector that can follow any existing diffusion sampler and increase its order of accuracy without additional model evaluations. They also derive UniP, a predictor supporting arbitrary order. Combining them produces UniPC, whose analytical form applies across orders. The approach improves numerical sampling accuracy while keeping costly network evaluations limited.

Experiments cover unconditional and conditional generation with both pixel-space and latent-space diffusion models. With ten function evaluations, UniPC achieves FID scores of 3.87 on unconditional CIFAR10 and 7.51 on conditional ImageNet at 256-by-256 resolution. The reported improvements are especially relevant when very few sampling steps are possible, showing how predictor–corrector design can improve quality within a tight evaluation budget.
neurips-2023-unipc-a-unified-predictor-c.tldr: UniPC accelerates diffusion sampling with a unified predictor–corrector design whose corrector improves accuracy without extra model evaluations.

paragraphs: Video chapters help viewers jump to information within long, untrimmed videos. Research on automatically producing them has been limited by a lack of public datasets. VidChapters-7M addresses this gap with 817,000 videos containing seven million chapters, collected from existing user annotations without additional manual labeling.

The paper defines three tasks that separate different parts of chapter creation. Full chapter generation requires finding segment boundaries and writing titles. A second task supplies the annotated boundaries and asks only for titles. Chapter grounding reverses that relationship: given an annotated title, the model must locate the corresponding interval in the video.

The authors evaluate simple baselines and state-of-the-art video-language models on all three tasks. They also show that pretraining on the dataset transfers well to dense video captioning, substantially improving the state of the art on YouCook2 and ViTT. Downstream performance improves with larger pretraining datasets in their experiments, supporting the value of scalable chapter collection for related video-understanding tasks.
neurips-2023-vidchapters-7m-video-chapte.tldr: VidChapters-7M supplies seven million user-created video chapters, three evaluation tasks, and evidence that chapter pretraining benefits dense video captioning.
